Using \(\quad \mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{F} / \mathrm{A}}{\Delta \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{L}}\)

questions.q: Assertion (a) : Ductile metals are used to prepare thin wires.Reason (R): In the stress-strain curve of ductile metals, the length between the points representing elastic limit and breaking point is very small.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. Ductile metals are materials that can be stretched or drawn into thin wires without breaking. This property, known as ductility, is essential for manufacturing wires for applications like electrical wiring and cables. Gold, silver, and copper are examples of highly ductile metals.
Reason (R) is false. The stress-strain curve for a ductile material has a long plastic deformation region between the elastic limit and the breaking point. This is precisely what defines a ductile material-it can undergo significant permanent deformation (plastic deformation) before it fractures. In contrast, a brittle material has a very small or non-existent plastic region, breaking soon after its elastic limit is reached.
The correct option is (3) (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Strain is a unit-less quantity.
Reason (R): Strain is equivalent to force.
options: Both \(A\) and \(R\) are true and \(R\) is the correct explanation of \(A\).
Both \(A\) and \(R\) are true but \(R\) is not the correct explanation of \(A\).
A is false but R is true.
questions.solution: Strain is defined as the ratio of change in dimensions of the body to the original dimensions. Since it is a ratio of two quantities with the same units, strain is indeed a unit-less quantity. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true. However, strain is a measure of deformation, while force is a push or pull. They are entirely different physical quantities and are not equivalent. Thus, Reason (R) is false.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>

Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is NOT the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is not correct
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is not correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is correct
questions.solution:
The relationship between Young's modulus, stress, and strain is:

stressstrain=Y

Since the elastic modulus of steel is more, for the same amount of stress, the strain will be less resulting in less deformation of buildings and bridges. Therefore, steel is used for construction of large structures. 

Hence, both assertion and reason are correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Ductile materials exhibit a large plastic deformation before fracture.
Reason (R): Ductile materials have a high Young's modulus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both \(A\) and \(R\) are true but \(R\) is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution: Ductile materials, by definition, can undergo significant plastic deformation (permanent change in shape) before they break. This means Assertion (A) is true. Young's modulus, however, is a measure of a material's stiffness or resistance to elastic deformation. A high Young's modulus indicates a stiff material, not necessarily a ductile one that undergoes large plastic deformation. Ductility is related to a material's ability to yield and deform plastically, which isn't directly measured by Young's modulus alone. Therefore, Reason (R) is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The stretching of a coil is determined by its shear modulus.
Reason (R): Shear modulus changes only the shape of a body, keeping its dimensions unchanged.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of \(A\).
A is true but R is false.
questions.solution: The stretching of a coil primarily involves a change in its length, which is governed by its Young's modulus (related to tensile or compressive stress), not its shear modulus. Shear modulus is associated with changes in the shape of a body due to shearing forces, where the dimensions remain largely unchanged. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false because stretching a coil is related to Young's modulus. Reason (R) is true as it correctly describes the effect of shear modulus on a body's shape without altering its dimensions.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Statement (A) For an ideal liquid, the bulk modulus is infinite and the shear modulus is zero.
Statement (B) The volume contraction of a metal cube of bulk modulus $140 \mathrm{GPa} .10 \mathrm{~cm}$ on a edge, when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of $7 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Pa}$ is $-0.05 \mathrm{~m}^3$.
Statement (C) A spiral spring is stretched by a weight attached to it. The strain is tensile.
options: A, B and C are true.
questions.solution:
For an ideal liquid, the bulk modulus, is infinite and shear modulus is zero.
Hence, statement (A) is correct.
In statement (B), Bulk modulus
$\begin{aligned}
B & =140 \mathrm{GPa} \\
& =140 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~Pa} \\
& =1.4 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{~Pa} \\
p & =7 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Pa} \\
V & =a^3=(0.1)^3 \\
& =0.001 \mathrm{~m}^3
\end{aligned}[a=10 \mathrm{~cm}=0.1 \mathrm{~m}]$
since, $\quad B=\frac{p}{\left(\frac{-\Delta V}{V}\right)}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 1.4 \times 10^{11}=\frac{7 \times 10^6}{\frac{-\Delta V}{0.001}} \\
& \Rightarrow 1.4 \times 10^{11}=\frac{7 \times 10^3}{-\Delta V}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow 1.4 \times 10^{11}=\frac{7 \times 10^3}{-\Delta V}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad \Delta V & =-\frac{7 \times 10^3}{1.4 \times 10^{11}} \\
& =-5 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~m}^3
\end{aligned}$
Hence, statement (B) is incorrect.
Strain produced in spiral spring stretched by a weight attached to it, is tensile.
Hence, statement $(C)$ is correct.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Elastomers possess a very high elastic limit.
Reason (R): Elastomers can be stretched to large deformations and still return to their original shape when the deforming force is removed.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.
questions.solution: Elastomers are materials like rubber that can be stretched to a very large extent without permanent deformation. This property is due to their molecular structure, allowing them to recover their original shape after the deforming force is removed, which is exactly what a high elastic limit implies. Therefore, both the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains why elastomers have a high elastic limit.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution: Breaking stress is a characteristic property of a material, representing the maximum stress it can endure before breaking, irrespective of its dimensions (length or cross sectional area). Therefore, Assertion (A) is true. Reason (R) correctly explains that breaking stress is an intrinsic property of the material, supporting why it's independent of length.

questions.q:
A copper wire \(\left(\mathrm{Y}=10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\right)\) of length 8 m and steel wire \(\left(\mathrm{Y}=2 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}\right)\) of length 4 m and each of cross-sectional area \(0.5 \mathrm{~cm}^2\) are fastened end to end and stretched with a tension of 500 N. Match the given columns and select the correct option from the codes given below.
\(\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Column-I} & \text{Column-II} \\
\text{(i) Elongation in copper wire (in mm)} & \text{(p) } 0.2 \\
\text{(ii) Elongation in steel wire (in mm)} & \text{(q) } 1.0 \\
\text{(iii) Total elongation (in mm)} & \text{(r) } 0.8
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
The pressure inside a soap bubble is inversely proportional to its radius (\(P_{ex} \propto \frac{1}{r})\). This means the smaller bubble (A) has a higher internal pressure than the larger bubble (B). When the valve V is opened, air will flow from the region of higher pressure (bubble A) to the region of lower pressure (bubble B).
As air flows out of A, its size will decrease, which further increases its internal pressure. As air flows into B, its size will increase, which decreases its internal pressure. This process will continue until bubble A becomes smaller and smaller, and bubble B becomes larger and larger.
Therefore, A will become smaller and B will become larger. This corresponds to option (3).

questions.q:
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column I} & & \text{Column II} \\
& \text{(Property)} &  &\text{(Description/Characteristic)} \\
\hline \text{(A)} & \text{Elasticity} & \text{(P)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Ability to retain} \\ \text{deformation after} \\ \text{stress is removed} \end{array} \\
\hline \text{(B)} & \text{Plasticity} & \text{(Q)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Maximum stress a} \\ \text{material can withstand} \\ \text{before breaking} \end{array} \\
\hline \text{(C)} & \text{Ductility} & \text{(R)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Tendency to regain} \\ \text{original shape after} \\ \text{deforming force is removed} \end{array} \\
\hline \text{(D)} & \text{Brittleness} & \text{(S)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Ability to be drawn} \\ \text{into thin wires} \end{array} \\
\hline \text{(E)} & \text{Tensile Strength} & \text{(T)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Breaks with little or} \\ \text{no plastic deformation} \end{array} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- (A) Elasticity \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\)
Elasticity = tendency to regain original shape after force is removed.
- (B) Plasticity \(\rightarrow\) (P)
Plasticity = ability to retain deformation after stress is removed. 
- (C) Ductility \(\rightarrow\) (S)
Ductility = ability to be drawn into thin wires. 
- (D) Brittleness \(\rightarrow\) (T)
Brittleness = breaks with little or no plastic deformation. 
- (E) Tensile Strength \(\rightarrow\) (Q)
Tensile strength = maximum stress material can withstand before breaking.
